title: Square-zero extensions of ring sheaves with specified additive kernel
statement: Let $T$ be a topological space, $f:R\to A$ a map of sheaves of commutative unital rings, and $G$ a module sheaf over $A$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A square-zero extension of $A$ as an $R$-algebra by $G$ consists of a sheaf of commutative unital rings $E$, ring-sheaf maps $b:R\to E$ and $p:E\to A$ with $pb=f$, and additive maps $i_U:G(U)\to E(U)$ commuting with restriction. Each $i_U$ is injective, $\ker p_U=\operatorname{im}i_U$, and $p$ is locally surjective for the open-cover topology. Require $i_U(g)i_U(h)=0$ and $e i_U(g)=i_U(p_U(e)g)$ for all local sections. A morphism over a coefficient map $v:G\to H$ is a ring-sheaf map $q:E\to F$ satisfying $qb_E=b_F$, $p_Fq=p_E$, and $qi_G=i_Hv$. An extension isomorphism is a ring-sheaf isomorphism satisfying these equations with $v=\mathrm{id}_G$. A split extension has an algebra section $s:A\to E$ of $p$; its coordinates $(a,g)\mapsto s(a)+i(g)$ have product $(a,g)(a',g')=(aa',ag'+a'g)$. A Baer diagram for $E_1,E_2,E_3$ is an $R$-algebra map $E_1\times_AE_2\to E_3$ over $A$ whose map on the kernel $G\oplus G$ is addition; equivalently it is given by maps on local pairs of equal quotient preserving restriction, addition, multiplication, unit, base and quotient, and sending $(i_1(g),i_2(h))$ to $i_3(g+h)$. Restriction of modules to an open $U$ uses the existing restriction to the localized site and its equivalence with sheaves on the open subspace. A restricted extension is identified with the restricted ring sheaf by an isomorphism respecting base, quotient and every restricted kernel section. These definitions assert no existence of extensions or diagrams.
